requirements.requirement: Treat node1's /etc/inventory/app.conf as authoritative and maintain a one-way synchronized copy on node2.
requirements.summary: A source-only change left node2 temporarily stale, then the synchronization job copied node1's content atomically to node2 with matching SHA-256 and content. Source-to-target parity was also demonstrated after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Automatically pick up changes from node1 on node2 within 15 minutes.
requirements.summary: Node2 had a running, boot-enabled crond service and a */15 schedule invoking the successfully tested synchronization job. However, the captured change was picked up by manually invoking that job six seconds later; no evidence directly observes crond triggering the job autonomously at a scheduled boundary.

overall_summary: The one-way synchronization mechanism works and remained healthy across sequential restarts, but the strict 15-minute automatic-pickup outcome is only partially proven because the tested source change was followed by a manual job invocation rather than an observed cron-triggered run. The provider-wide restart protocol is otherwise strong for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered services, data, schedule, and source/target parity.
limitations: No captured command observes crond itself launching the synchronization job after a source change, so autonomous pickup within the promised interval remains indirectly supported by configuration.
Alpine lacks the lifecycle collector's systemd failed-unit check; service recovery was instead directly checked with OpenRC commands.
The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the task-specific configuration files or accounts, so their persistence is established primarily by executor commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related mutations had clear roles: creating the initially absent source, provisioning dedicated access, installing and enabling the synchronization job, making a bounded verification change, and performing the mandatory restart checks. The only unnecessary retained mutations were /tmp/inventory-reboot.log files left on node1 and node2 by the reboot scheduling commands; neither was cleaned up. Package-health output was unchanged and post-task socket observations showed no new listening service class.
